question: What is the authoritative Sa2020 inclusion population: PlaViSca's 9766 STARsolo-filtered cells, the publication's 9215-cell main analysis, or a tiered scheme?

evidence: sa2020_main_analysis_cell_lineage.tsv, sa2020_lower_threshold_cell_lineage.tsv: 9018 overlap, 748 extra, 197 missing from PlaViSca
downstream_consequence: Choosing (a) changes cell membership (selecting the existing 9018-overlap subset requires no raw reprocessing) -> full downstream normalization/integration/annotation regeneration; choosing (c) also changes cell membership and may additionally require raw reprocessing to recover the 197 missing cells -> same full downstream regeneration, plus FASTQ/alignment-level work if needed; (b) is metadata-only (tag as covariate, no membership change) -> no downstream normalization/integration/annotation regeneration, only export regeneration for the new covariate column
recommendation: Adopt (b): retain 9766 as primary population but add an explicit main_analysis_member boolean covariate; this is metadata-only and preserves maximal information while being transparent about the QC-definition difference

question: How should Ruberto2022_1's 538 near-empty-expression replicate-2 cells be repaired: realign/reprocess, substitute author-derived counts, or flag/exclude?
alternatives: (a) Investigate FASTQ/STARsolo alignment logs for SRR19573609/SRR19573610 first, then realign if a fixable technical fault is found; (b) substitute the authors' own local-object counts for these 538 cell IDs (byte-level provenance of that author object is unresolved); (c) flag and retain with a caveat, or exclude, without further reprocessing
evidence: near_empty_cells_vs_hep59.tsv: authors' object shows real signal (median nCount_RNA 718.5) for the identical cell IDs; PlaViSca's own STARsolo-vs-study-object concordance is exact, ruling out an R-level import bug; UPDATE 2026-09-20 (ruberto2022_1/D036_resolution.md): option (a) was pursued to completion - a controlled kallisto|bustools re-alignment (the authors' own successful methodology) of the content-verified local FASTQ found abundant parasite-mappable signal in 609/610 but none of it attributable to the 538 known real-cell barcodes (same null result as STARsolo), while the identical method correctly recovers strong signal at the known real cells of the unaffected control runs 611/612. This rules out reprocessing (option a) as a viable repair path with the public deposit's current content.
downstream_consequence: (a) requires raw reprocessing and full downstream regeneration for these cells (and likely the whole study, then the atlas); (b) requires establishing byte-level provenance of the author object first, then a targeted count substitution plus downstream regeneration; (c) is a metadata/inclusion-only change
recommendation: Pursue (a) first (investigate STARsolo Summary.csv/alignment logs to root-cause the implausibly large barcode space and low per-cell UMI pattern in the two affected runs); fall back to (c) explicit flagging if reprocessing does not resolve the issue within a reasonable effort; do not pursue (b) without first resolving the author object's Zenodo provenance UPDATE 2026-09-20: pursue (c)/explicit flagging (already implemented: near_empty_expression_flag, total_umi_count) rather than further reprocessing; option (a) has now been tried with a fundamentally different, more sensitive method and failed at the cell-barcode level, not merely the aggregate-signal level. Option (b) (author-object substitution) evaluated in D036_resolution.md Part 10: provenance is now well-documented but still requires explicit project-lead sign-off before use, since it would mix two different alignment methodologies within one study's population. UPDATE 2026-09-20 (Phase 2, project-lead decision, FINAL): the project lead has formally decided to adopt option (b) for the complete 1,438-cell Ruberto2022_1 population (not only the 538 D036-affected cells): use the complete author-derived raw UMI matrix (data/Hep59.1.2.seu_20aug2025.rds, RNA counts layer) for ALL 1,438 cells, not just the 538 previously near-empty ones, so that the study is internally consistent on a single counting pipeline rather than mixing STARsolo counts (900 cells) with author kallisto/bustools counts (538 cells) within one study. Rationale: (1) public FASTQ/STARsolo reconstruction is confirmed not reproducible for the 538 cells (D036_resolution.md); (2) independent kallisto reprocessing of the same FASTQ did not rescue them either - the defect is upstream of alignment method; (3) the author RNA counts layer is confirmed non-negative integer raw UMI counts (rna_counts_validation.tsv); (4) the exact 1,438-cell crosswalk is one-to-one with zero unmapped/duplicate IDs (cell_crosswalk_validation.tsv); (5) the 900 unaffected cells show strong positive expression/cell-identity concordance between the author matrix and PlaViScas own STARsolo reconstruction (cell_identity_test.tsv: rank-1 match 85-100% depending on run vs 0.16-0.39% chance rate), supporting that the author matrix for the unaffected cells measures the same biological cells, not a different/relabeled population; (6) all 4,722 author PVP01 gene IDs map exactly and unambiguously into PlaViScas 6,811-feature panel (author_gene_mapping.tsv). Explicit residual caveat retained, NOT resolved by this decision: byte-level identity of the local dated object (Hep59.1.2.seu_20aug2025.rds) to the canonical Zenodo-deposited RDS remains unconfirmed - this is a provenance completeness caveat, not a reason to distrust the validated counts, and is recorded in count_provenance_status for all affected cells. This decision replaces D036/DEC09 as an open blocker: it is no longer a blocker for Phase 2, since the scientific sign-off is now given; implementation proceeds in scripts/ruberto2022_1_pv_analysis_script.R using the author RNA counts layer for all 1,438 cells, explicit source_of_counts/counting_pipeline/count_reference_version/count_provenance_status metadata, and zero-fill ONLY the 2,089 PlaViSca features confirmed/inferred structurally absent from the author reference (see phase2_feature_coverage.tsv), never interpreting reference-absent genes as unconditional biological zero without that evidence trail.

question: Should the post-integration "male/female gametocyte AND Anopheles host" cell-removal step be retained, redesigned, or removed entirely?
alternatives: (a) Remove the filter entirely, since it can delete source-defined cells based solely on a downstream classifier's incompatible output; (b) retain but gate strictly on source-defined tissue/population type rather than solely on classifier output, and log every removed cell; (c) retain unchanged
evidence: singleR.R L142-146 (source/run override) vs L329-331 (later, unconditional gametocyte-cluster override, see D045) vs L460-465 (filter): currently 0 cells are actually removed today, but only because no known Anopheles-host cell currently lands in the gametocyte cluster after both overrides run in sequence - the later cluster override can re-overwrite the earlier Sporozoite relabeling for any cell (known or future) whose expression profile clusters as gametocyte, making the current zero-removal outcome a data accident, not a structural guarantee
downstream_consequence: (a)/(b) are logic-only for currently-known studies (zero deployed removals observed today) but (b) requires an explicit logging mechanism and must be implemented together with the D045 fix (scoping the gametocyte-cluster override to skip source-selection-defined stages), since D049's filter alone cannot be made safe while D045 remains unfixed; (c) leaves both the ordering risk and the latent data-loss risk unaddressed
recommendation: Adopt (b): gate the filter on tissue_or_sample_type/source_stage_provenance rather than solely on classifier output, log every cell ever removed with its ID, study, and reason, and apply the D045 override-scoping fix in the same change so the source-selection-defined Sporozoite relabeling can no longer be silently undone before this filter runs

question: Given that IntegrateLayers/HarmonyIntegration's group_by="study_label" is confirmed non-functional (grouping is actually derived from per-merged-object layer structure), should the atlas continue to use one single global Harmony integration, or move to a stratified/hierarchical scheme?
alternatives: (a) Keep one global integration, but fix the code so the intended grouping (by study, or by a more principled biological/technical covariate) is genuinely achieved; (b) move to a stratified/hierarchical integration (e.g. integrate within comparable tissue/lifecycle groups first, then across); (c) keep the current code as-is, documenting the coincidental correctness
evidence: Confounding is severe: Hazzard2024 alone contributes ~75.5% of all cells; the six studies differ simultaneously in lifecycle stage, host/tissue, technology, and condition
downstream_consequence: (a) requires a full atlas-wide Harmony/clustering/SingleR/gametocyte rerun; (b) requires the same rerun plus a redesigned integration architecture and additional validation; (c) leaves a scientifically risky, currently-unvalidated integration in production
recommendation: Adopt (a) as the immediate fix (make the grouping mechanism genuinely correspond to study, since that was always the stated intent) and treat (b) as a longer-term research question to be evaluated using the acceptance-test validation metrics in acceptance_tests.tsv (batch mixing only within biologically comparable populations, neighbor composition by study/biology) before committing to a single global scheme for publication

question: How should the reproducibility problem of hard-coded numeric cluster-to-sex-label mapping be solved?
alternatives: (a) Redesign as an automated, marker-score-threshold-based classification (not depending on arbitrary cluster numbering); (b) keep manual cluster inspection after every rerun, but add a mandatory marker-driven verification step before RenameIdents is applied; (c) drop cluster-based sex calling entirely and rely solely on author-provided sex annotations where available

recommendation: Adopt (b) as a near-term interim safeguard (mandatory verification step) and pursue (a) as the target design; do not adopt (c) outright since author sex labels are unavailable for most of the atlas
